arches-canyonlands.overview: The hiking here explores two distinct desert landscapes: the concentrated sandstone fins and windows of Arches, and the vast, deep gorges of Canyonlands. Most routes are day hikes across bare slickrock, leading to iconic formations like Delicate Arch or the canyon rims at Island in the Sky. The Needles district offers longer, rugged day hikes and multi-day routes through colorful sandstone spires. The labyrinth of the Fiery Furnace requires a specific permit to enter.

months.1: Winter brings freezing temperatures and occasional snow, which makes the slickrock trails icy and slow. The main paths remain open for prepared walkers.
months.5: Peak hiking weather, with warm, dry days perfect for the canyon descents and long slickrock loops before the intense heat arrives.
months.6: Highs climb into the 90s and can top 100°F, making the exposed sandstone dangerous by midday. Hikers must start at dawn and finish the long routes by mid-morning.
months.9: The heat begins to ease, though afternoons remain very warm. Early starts are still recommended for long hikes like the Devils Garden loop.

months.7: High heat and humidity make the woodland loops sticky and tiring in the afternoon sun.

madeira.overview: Madeira is famous for its levadas, a network of irrigation channels more than 1,000 miles long, with hiking paths beside them through laurel forest and along cliffs, including a waterfall hike at Caldeirão Verde. The steep ridge hike from Pico do Arieiro to Pico Ruivo, 6,110 ft, earns views of the island's jagged volcanic spine when the cloud lifts. Winter brings rain and cloud to the heights; spring and early autumn are best.

months.1: Winter brings more rain and cloud to the high peaks, making the ridge routes slippery and less rewarding. The lower levada paths stay green, though walkers should expect occasional showers.
months.2: Winter brings more rain and cloud to the high peaks, making the ridge routes slippery and less rewarding. The lower levada paths stay green, though walkers should expect occasional showers.
months.12: Winter brings more rain and cloud to the high peaks, making the ridge routes slippery and less rewarding. The lower levada paths stay green, though walkers should expect occasional showers.

months.3: Spring weather arrives, making the steep scramble up Cathedral Rock ideal.
months.5: The desert warms up quickly, so the unshaded climbs to the high viewpoints are best tackled in the early morning.
months.9: The intense heat begins to break, reopening the longer climbs to the high mesas as the summer storms fade.

months.7: High heat and intense humidity make the climbs exhausting; start at dawn or use the cable cars to reach the shaded ridges.

banff.overview: Glacier-carved valleys and jagged peaks surround trails for every level, with a gondola to the alpine meadows at Sunshine. Multi-day routes like the 27-mile, 3-day Skyline Trail cross high passes, while day hikes range from easy lakeshore paths to steep climbs. In July and August the parks are crowded, especially at Moraine Lake, Lake Louise and Johnston Canyon, where parking fills early, so Moraine Lake and Lake Louise now need shuttle reservations. The best conditions run from late June to September.

months.6: The hiking season opens as snow melts from the middle elevations, though high passes and multi-day treks often hold snow until late in the month.

months.5: Heat builds in the lower valleys and haze and pre-monsoon clouds often obscure the peaks by midday, making early starts essential. The high-altitude routes remain open, but the window for clear panoramas narrows.
months.10: The absolute best time for Himalayan trekking, with washed-clean skies delivering unmatched views of the highest peaks. The high passes are clear, the weather is stable, and the multi-day routes are in perfect condition.

torres-del-paine.overview: Granite towers, glaciers and turquoise lakes surround the trails here. Day hikes start from trailheads reached by bus or catamaran, while the famous W Trek (about 40 miles in 4 to 6 days) and O Circuit (about 80 miles in 7 to 9 days) offer long multi-day routes between refugios. The weather is notoriously windy, and the main trekking window runs from October to April when the trails and huts are fully open.

months.1: The peak month for the W and O treks, with long daylight hours and all refugios open. Expect the region's famous fierce winds, but the trails to the granite towers and glaciers are fully accessible.
months.3: Daylight begins to shorten and temperatures drop, but the trails and refugios remain fully open. The winds often ease slightly, making the climbs to the viewpoints highly rewarding.
months.10: All refugios open and the full W and O treks are available again. The weather is highly unpredictable and winds pick up, but the routes to the granite towers are clear.
months.11: Long daylight hours return and the trails are in excellent condition. The multi-day circuits and day hikes are fully operational, though the famous winds are a constant factor.
months.12: One of the best months to hike the W and O treks, with maximum daylight for the long days on the trail. All boat and shuttle access to the trailheads is running.

aspen.overview: The Elk Mountains offer high-altitude trails past alpine lakes and jagged peaks, with the best views reached by a mandatory shuttle to the Maroon Bells trailhead. Day hikes range from easy valley loops to steep climbs, while the Four Pass Loop is a strenuous 26-mile trek over four days. The best-known trails are crowded in summer, requiring timed reservations for the shuttle and parking. The main hiking season runs from July to September when the high passes are clear of snow.

months.7: The high passes are clear, opening the multi-day treks and high alpine day hikes, though the best-known trailheads are crowded and require timed reservations.
months.8: Summer weather keeps the entire network open for high-altitude hikes and treks, with crowded trailheads and mandatory shuttle reservations still in effect.
months.9: The aspen trees turn gold, offering spectacular scenery on the valley trails, while the high passes remain clear for treks before the first autumn snows.

months.5: Heat and humidity rise noticeably, making the exposed coastal paths tiring by midday.

big-island.overview: The Big Island offers a unique mix of volcanic landscapes and coastal trails, from the stark lava fields of Hawai'i Volcanoes National Park to the lush valleys of the north coast. The steep hike down into Waipi'o Valley or the trails around Kilauea's caldera show off scenery that can only be reached on foot. The dry season from May to September is the most reliable time to walk, especially on the rainier eastern side.

months.5: The dry season begins, making this a great time for the valley hikes and the caldera trails before the peak summer heat sets in.
months.9: The reliable dry season holds, offering excellent conditions for the valley descents and the volcanic craters before the autumn rains return.

bordeaux.overview: Bordeaux is known for wine rather than wilderness, but easy walking trails thread through the surrounding vineyards and along the Atlantic coast an hour away. Good walking options include loops through the estates of Saint-Émilion or the sandy coastal paths near Arcachon Bay.

months.7: Summer heat makes the unshaded vineyard trails tiring by midday, so early starts are best.

months.6: Heat builds quickly, making the exposed trails hard going by midday; early morning starts are essential for any day hike.
months.8: The extreme heat and fire danger continue at their peak, keeping the mountain trails largely off-limits or too hot to enjoy.

atacama.overview: The high-altitude desert offers stark, otherworldly day hikes through slot canyons and jagged rock formations. The best-known routes explore the Valle de la Luna, where trails wind past sand dunes and salt-crusted cliffs, and the Guatin Canyon, known for its giant cacti. Tickets for popular areas must be bought in advance if not hiking as part of a guided itinerary.

argentine-lake-district.overview: The Argentine Lake District is known for its mountain trails that climb steeply through southern beech forests to reach granite spires and alpine lakes. The hiking centers on Nahuel Huapi National Park near Bariloche, where a large network of mountain huts supports multi-day treks. Well known destinations include Refugio Frey, where the trail climbs to a cirque of jagged peaks and a high lake. A free national park registration is required for the trails, and the refugios must be booked in advance.

azores.overview: Volcanic craters, coastal cliffs and lush laurel forests define the hiking on these mid-Atlantic islands. The best-known route is the steep climb up Mount Pico on Pico island, Portugal's highest peak, with panoramic ocean views. Other highlights are the trails around the Caldeira crater on Faial and the paths circling the twin lakes of Sete Cidades on São Miguel. The trails are walkable year-round, though rain frequently obscures the heights.

months.6: Long daylight hours and mostly clear skies provide excellent conditions for the high volcanic routes. The steep climb up Mount Pico rewards hikers with expansive mid-Atlantic views, while the coastal paths remain breezy.
months.7: The most reliable weather of the year keeps the high crater rims and the Mount Pico trail clear of cloud. The paths around Sete Cidades and Faial's Caldeira offer expansive views over the lakes and the ocean.
months.8: The most reliable weather of the year keeps the high crater rims and the Mount Pico trail clear of cloud. The paths around Sete Cidades and Faial's Caldeira offer expansive views over the lakes and the ocean.
months.9: The trails remain largely dry and the volcanic slopes are bright green. The ascent of Mount Pico and the trails around Faial's Caldeira crater offer excellent visibility and steady walking conditions.
months.11: Heavy rain and low visibility make the high routes like Mount Pico slippery and unrewarding. Walkers stick to the sheltered laurel forests and coastal paths, which stay walkable despite the wet conditions.

months.2: The heavy rains continue, keeping the mountain paths slick and slow, though the paved walks around the rice terraces remain easy.
months.6: Excellent conditions for walking, with firm trails and clear, cool mornings that reward the early start on the crater hikes.
months.9: The trails remain dry and the mornings clear, keeping the volcano climbs and jungle walks in great condition.

months.2: Monsoon rains begin to ease, though jungle paths remain slick and muddy. The Kinabalu summit route opens more frequently, but conditions are still wet and tiring.

months.6: Early summer provides warm, clear days for exploring the Buda Hills, though midday heat can make the climbs tiring.
Summer heat sets in, making the unshaded coastal paths hard going by midday. Start early to finish before the afternoon heat.

andalucia.overview: Hiking ranges from the high peaks of the Sierra Nevada to deep limestone gorges. The famous Caminito del Rey is a point to point hike including sections of suspended boardwalk pinned to the sheer walls of the Gaitanes Gorge. This walk requires a timed ticket, and most visitors take a shuttle to the start. The high mountains offer strenuous day hikes to summits like Mulhacén. The hiking is best in spring and autumn, as summer heat is extreme.

months.3: Temperatures rise significantly, making exposed trails and jungle routes much harder work.
months.8: Deep into the wet months, most unpaved trails are waterlogged and the longer routes are largely washed out.

acadia.overview: Granite peaks rise straight from the Atlantic, offering a dense network of day hikes that range from easy lake loops to iron-rung scrambles up the cliffs. Hikers reach the trailheads by driving or using the park's shuttle system. The park is heavily crowded from summer through October, especially at the Jordan Pond and Cadillac Mountain trailheads, where parking fills early and driving up Cadillac Summit Road needs a reservation.

months.5: Spring brings clear trails and moderate temperatures. The iron-rung routes are open and the summer crowds have not yet arrived.

months.2: Clear skies and lower humidity make this an ideal time for climbs to canopy viewpoints. The paths are dry and footing is reliable.
months.4: Temperatures rise significantly, making the jungle climbs much hotter. The trails remain dry, but the heat requires carrying extra water.
months.6: The wet season begins, bringing heavy afternoon downpours. Trails quickly become muddy and slick, making steep sections slow.
months.11: The rains begin to ease, but the forest paths remain slick and muddy. The longer waterfall hikes are still slow going due to poor footing.

belize.overview: Belize offers tropical forest trails leading to hidden waterfalls and sweeping jungle canopy views. The best day hikes are in the Cockscomb Basin Wildlife Sanctuary, a jaguar reserve where the Tiger Fern Trail climbs to a double waterfall, and at Mayflower Bocawina National Park, where a rope-assisted climb ends at Antelope Falls and its swimming pools. The dry months provide the most reliable footing, as heavy rains quickly turn the clay trails slick.

months.4: Intense heat makes trekking exhausting; early morning starts are essential to avoid the worst of the afternoon sun. Burning-season smoke can linger.

bend-crater-lake.overview: The volcanic landscapes of Central Oregon offer routes ranging from loops along the deep blue waters of Crater Lake to challenging ascents in the high Cascades. Walkers can explore easy paths along the Deschutes River near Bend or tackle the strenuous climb up South Sister for panoramic views of glaciers and cinder cones. Central Cascades wilderness permits are required for many of the best high-elevation mountain routes from mid-June to mid-October.

months.6: High-elevation trails begin to clear of snow, though patches remain on the mountain routes. Central Cascades wilderness permits are required starting mid-month.
months.7: The high passes and Crater Lake rim trails are fully clear, offering summit hikes and caldera views. The weather is warm and dry, and Central Cascades wilderness permits are required.
months.8: The high passes and Crater Lake rim trails are fully clear, offering summit hikes and caldera views. The weather is warm and dry, and Central Cascades wilderness permits are required. Wildfire smoke is most likely now, so check air quality before heading up.
months.9: The high passes and Crater Lake rim trails are clear, offering summit hikes and caldera views. The weather is warm and dry, and Central Cascades wilderness permits are required. Wildfire smoke can still haze the air early in the month.
months.10: Frost and early snowfalls begin to close the highest routes, making mountain hikes icy. Central Cascades wilderness permits are required until mid-month.

months.7: High heat makes the exposed ridge trails hard going. The shaded Valle delle Ferriere offers a cooler alternative under the forest canopy.

barcelona.overview: The best hiking lies just outside the city, with the serrated peaks of Montserrat offering steep day hikes to the Sant Jeroni summit for views stretching to the Pyrenees. Closer in, the wooded ridges of the Collserola range provide trails above the city, easily reached by funicular or train. The Mediterranean climate makes hiking possible year-round, though summer afternoons are intensely hot.

months.4: Ideal hiking weather with comfortable temperatures for the longer routes and clear views from the ridges.
months.5: Ideal hiking weather with comfortable temperatures for the longer routes and clear views from the ridges.
months.7: Intense summer heat makes the long trails difficult; the shaded paths in Collserola are the best option for a short walk.
months.10: Ideal hiking weather returns with comfortable temperatures for the longer routes and clear views from the ridges.

beijing.overview: The hiking here is defined by the Great Wall, offering routes along ancient stone paths and crumbling watchtowers that trace the mountain ridges. Visitors typically take a shuttle or cable car to reach restored sections like Mutianyu and Jinshanling for day hikes, while wild stretches like Jiankou offer steep scrambling over crumbling wall. The best hiking is in spring and autumn when the air is clear and temperatures are mild.

months.1: Bitterly cold winds sweep across the exposed ridges, making the steep stone steps icy and slow. The restored sections remain open for those prepared for freezing temperatures. Winter heating-season smog often leaves the air poor.
months.5: The mild, clear weather continues, providing ideal conditions for scrambles on the wild sections and walks on the restored walls.
months.6: Summer heat and humidity begin to build, making the steep climbs much harder work. Haze often obscures the distant ridge views.
months.8: The hot and humid conditions persist, keeping the steep climbs hard work and sweaty. Afternoon showers are common, so early morning starts are essential.

belfast-giants-causeway.overview: The coastal cliffs and heather-covered granite peaks offer strong regional hiking, anchored by the Causeway Coast Way, a 33-mile trek over two to three days past basalt columns and ruined castles. Day hikers head to the Mourne Mountains for steep climbs up Slieve Donard, or the Glens of Antrim for forest and waterfall loops. The trails are best from May to September, though rain is possible year-round.

months.1: Winter brings short daylight, high winds, and boggy ground in the mountains, leaving the peaks hard going and exposed. The lower coastal paths remain walkable but require full rain gear.
months.2: The mountains remain wet and boggy with frequent high winds, keeping the high ridges hard going and exposed. Coastal walks offer dramatic scenery between winter storms.
months.5: The longest days and driest weather of the year make this the best time for the coastal trek and mountain climbs. The heather is in bloom, and the cliffside paths offer clear views across the water.
months.6: The longest days and driest weather of the year make this the best time for the coastal trek and mountain climbs. The heather is in bloom, and the cliffside paths offer clear views across the water.
months.7: The longest days and driest weather of the year make this the best time for the coastal trek and mountain climbs. The heather is in bloom, and the cliffside paths offer clear views across the water.
months.8: The longest days and driest weather of the year make this the best time for the coastal trek and mountain climbs. The heather is in bloom, and the cliffside paths offer clear views across the water.
months.11: Shortening daylight and frequent storms leave the high peaks heavily exposed. Walkers stick to the lower coastal paths and sheltered glens, which stay open year-round.
months.12: Winter brings short daylight, high winds, and boggy ground in the mountains, leaving the peaks hard going and exposed. The lower coastal paths remain walkable but require full rain gear.

bhutan.overview: Bhutan offers some of the most dramatic and remote hiking in the Himalayas, from steep forest day hikes to legendary high-altitude expedition treks. The steep climb to the cliffside Tiger's Nest monastery is the best known day hike, while the multi-week Snowman Trek and the shorter Druk Path Trek cross remote passes beneath unclimbed peaks. All hiking requires a licensed guide and a daily fee, keeping the trails pristine. The best hiking is in spring and autumn.

months.4: One of the best months to walk here. The high passes are accessible, the weather is mild, and the multi-day treks offer spectacular views of the Himalayan peaks.

months.9: Excellent conditions continue with clear skies and cooler air, perfect for gorge hikes and multi-day routes.

bavaria-munich.overview: The real hiking is about an hour and a half south of the city in the Bavarian Alps, where trains and cable cars lift hikers to high ridge trails above alpine lakes. The network around Garmisch and Mittenwald offers everything from easy valley loops to rugged limestone summits and multi-day hut-to-hut routes.

months.4: Spring clears the forest and lake trails, while the high-elevation routes remain closed by snow and ice.
months.6: The high ridge trails and hut-to-hut routes open as the last snow melts, offering excellent high-level hiking.
months.9: The high trails remain clear and crisp, making this an ideal time for ridge hikes.
months.10: Autumn colors fill the valleys and trails are excellent, though early snow can close the highest routes.

borabora.overview: French Polynesia offers rugged, steep jungle trails leading to volcanic viewpoints, though the network is modest. On Bora Bora, the steep scramble up Mount Pahia requires a guide, while the shoulder of Mount Otemanu offers a challenging day hike beneath the sheer summit cliffs. The best hiking is found from May to October when the paths are drier and less slippery.

months.1: Heavy rain and high heat make the steep jungle paths extremely slippery and slow. Occasional cyclone risk can close trails entirely.
months.2: Heavy rain and high heat make the steep jungle paths extremely slippery and slow. Occasional cyclone risk can close trails entirely.
months.5: Drier weather arrives, making the steep ascent up Mount Pahia much safer. The humidity drops, improving the steep climbs.
months.11: The wetter weather sets in, turning the steep dirt paths slick. Heat and humidity make the steep climbs much harder.

badlands-black-hills.overview: The region offers two distinct landscapes for day hikers: the exposed, eroded pinnacles of the Badlands and the shaded ponderosa pine forests of the Black Hills. Trails range from easy prairie loops to the climb up Black Elk Peak, which rewards hikers with views of granite spires. The 111-mile Centennial Trail provides a multi-day trek through the hills and plains. Spring and autumn offer the most reliable weather across both areas.

months.8: Late summer heat keeps the Badlands trails hot and exposed by midday. The Black Hills remain the best option for comfortable day hikes.

berlin.overview: Berlin is a flat city, but the forests and lakes on its edges offer easy, shaded walking. The Grunewald forest and the paths along the Havel river provide miles of wide trails under the trees, reachable by train.

cape-town.overview: Table Mountain and the Cape Peninsula offer outstanding day hikes right above the city, from easy coastal and fynbos paths around Cape Point to steep scrambles up the mountain's sandstone cliffs. The hiking is best from March to May and from September to November, when the weather is mild.

months.1: The trails are dry and the days are hot, so start the climbs before dawn to beat the heat.
